A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 14-page versions of the same V-Skip paper, including Appendices A–C. Text and visual inspection support comparison throughout; pages 3–14 have identical extracted text and rendered images.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark, efficiency, hallucination, and ablation results in Section 4, plus visual-layer and LoRA-rank sensitivity experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original empirical results on MMMU, DocVQA, and POPE, together with the appendix sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: The dual-path scoring, Union-of-Saliency gate, offline rationale compression, and LoRA distillation remain identical in Section 3 and Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same MMMU reasoning, DocVQA document-understanding, and balanced POPE hallucination tasks. No datasets, domains, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Original (Full), Truncation, LLMLingua-2, and ASCoT as comparators. Comparator membership in the attribute-retention, POPE, and component analyses also matches.

E3.justification: The MMMU and DocVQA validation splits, model configurations, compression ratios, metrics, and training settings are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix B.

E4.justification: The scaling, attribute-retention, invoice case, hallucination, and gating analyses are unchanged. Appendix C retains identical visual-layer and LoRA-rank sensitivity studies.

E5.justification: Both versions retain identical point-estimate reporting, without reported repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All results in Tables 1–7 and Figures 4–6 match. For example, Table 1 reports the same 48.2% MMMU accuracy and 83.7% DocVQA ANLS for V-Skip on Qwen2-VL-7B at a target compression ratio of 0.5.

T1.justification: The VA-IB objective, entropy decomposition, attention-based scoring definitions, and retention-mask formulation in Section 3 are identical. No mathematical definitions, derivations, assumptions, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions and claims concerning Visual Amnesia, VA-IB, visual grounding, and the claimed 2.9× inference speedup.

C2.justification: Interpretations of entropy mismatch, model-size robustness, and grounding-versus-fluency tradeoffs are unchanged. Both versions retain the limitations concerning dependence on base-model alignment and offline-distillation overhead.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains identical implementation and reproducibility details, including LoRA rank 16, three training epochs, optimizer settings, and eight RTX 3090 GPUs. Code and data access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list are unchanged. The positioning of V-Skip relative to text-centric compression and other multimodal reasoning work is also retained.

P1.justification: v3 adds an equal-contribution marker to Cheng Tan, adjusts author-note punctuation, and updates the arXiv version/date text. The substantive prose and section ordering remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The equal-contribution note moves from beneath the author information to a first-page footnote, causing limited text reflow on pages 1–2. Figures and tables are unchanged, and pages 3–14 render identically.

improvement.justification: The scientific argument, empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information are identical, including the appendices. Revised equal-contribution attribution and minor opening-page layout changes produce no meaningful net difference in the paper's overall quality.
